title: object ownership and tenant separation
use_when: an operation reads a named user's record, document or other owned object.
expected_artifacts: reviewed case, per-identity execution evidence, triage candidate if access disagrees, and a reviewed finding only after verification.
prerequisites: Choose the engagement, client and written authorization. Review the testing window, permitted targets and stop-work. Policy warnings are advisory; the operator decides whether the traffic is permitted.
Use dedicated identities and disposable objects with known permissions. Use value_env or value_keychain references, never token values.
Establish a working legitimate baseline. Rate limits, redirects, transport failures and stale credentials remain inconclusive. Mutations require explicit execution opt-in.
steps: Capture the successful owner request with the Burp extension or POST /engagements/{id}/api/exchanges; inspect it in Review → API Surface. Confirm the actual owner/object and tenant from the agreed test data.

Draft a case through the case builder or POST /engagements/{id}/test-cases/preview. Select owner, same-tenant non-owner, other-tenant user, anonymous caller and an administrator if one is applicable. A draft's skip decisions must be reviewed; do not infer permissions from a successful response or the identity's name.

Set each expected decision, credential reference and resource ownership/tenant context. Declare real denial conventions, such as 404 for hidden objects or deny_when.json_field for an HTTP 200 error body. Save through the reviewed case builder or test-cases save --reviewed.

Queue vardrgate_api_test with the stored test_case_id. For a loopback lab, private-target opt-in is the local Runner operator's choice; it cannot be granted by backend configuration. Review actual execution statuses and outcomes, not just the job's completion badge or finding count.

Verify any potential_bola, cross_tenant_access or missing_authentication candidate with a legitimate baseline and protected response structure. Rule out public data, session expiry, a wrong object and documented delegated access. Promote only a verified issue to a finding.
common_traps: an error body behind HTTP 200; the wrong tenant; a login redirect; API keys accidentally pasted into case JSON; a multi-parameter URL changed by escaping; testing page 1 and claiming an entire collection; overreading a single case as methodology coverage. The fixture exercises vulnerable and fixed controls, declared 404/body denials, stale credentials, two pages and query preservation.
manual_remainder: deciding intended permissions and business impact, object lifecycle/alias/batch variants, delegated access and write authorization. Gate does not infer these from a response.

title: privileged functions
use_when: an administrative operation should be restricted by role.
expected_artifacts: reviewed role expectations, legitimate admin baseline and evidence for each tested identity.
prerequisites: Choose the engagement, client and written authorization. Review the testing window, permitted targets and stop-work. Policy warnings are advisory; the operator decides whether the traffic is permitted.
Use dedicated identities and disposable objects with known permissions. Use value_env or value_keychain references, never token values.
Establish a working legitimate baseline. Rate limits, redirects, transport failures and stale credentials remain inconclusive. Mutations require explicit execution opt-in.
steps: Identify an admin operation from observed traffic or an API specification. Verify it is a privileged function; an /admin path alone is insufficient.

Choose the actual administrator, lower-role caller and anonymous identity; include tenant variants when roles are tenant-bound. Review allow/deny for each caller. Set resource.required_role and the intended role_hierarchy.
Prefer a read-only operation first. For mutations, use disposable objects and review the effects of repeating the request per identity before enabling them.

Queue the saved Gate case. Verify the admin baseline and inspect the lower-role execution. A privilege_escalation candidate needs a confirmed unauthorized capability or protected response, not merely a shared status code.
Repeat the same case after remediation and compare both runs. Keep failed, blocked and inconclusive executions visible.
common_traps: stale administrator credentials; interpreting a generic success envelope as the privileged operation; applying a global role hierarchy to a tenant-specific role; performing the mutation multiple times unintentionally. The fixture checks both vulnerable and fixed admin functions.
manual_remainder: workflow/state changes, role delegation, background jobs and impacts that require observing side effects beyond one response.

title: evidence, retest and client handoff
use_when: a candidate is verified and needs a durable assessment record.
expected_artifacts: reviewed finding, linked evidence, finding activity, retest evidence and an immutable client deliverable revision.
prerequisites: Choose the engagement, client and written authorization. Review the testing window, permitted targets and stop-work. Policy warnings are advisory; the operator decides whether the traffic is permitted.
Use dedicated identities and disposable objects with known permissions. Use value_env or value_keychain references, never token values.
Establish a working legitimate baseline. Rate limits, redirects, transport failures and stale credentials remain inconclusive. Mutations require explicit execution opt-in.
steps: Review the candidate and create the finding with reproduction, impact and remediation. Select execution evidence by job_id, case_id and identity_id; preserve its content hash and source. Historical or manual records without provenance must be identified by the operator.

Link the evidence through the Evidence UI or POST /engagements/{id}/evidence/{evidence_id}/link. A linked record cannot be moved to another finding; it should remain an account of the original observation.

Record retest activity with the actual outcome and selected linked evidence. After remediation, replay the reviewed case and link its new evidence. Use verified_fixed only after the legitimate baseline still works and previously unauthorized identities receive the intended denial.

In Reports, create an engagement client report. Review scope, authorization, selected findings/evidence, methodology and limitations before committing a revision. Internal per-finding write-ups are separate records.
Download/review the report. Later source edits do not rewrite a saved revision; make a new revision when retest or editorial content changes.
common_traps: calling a transport failure fixed; reporting "OWASP covered" because a tool ran; citing the wrong run's evidence; mixing a draft write-up with a client deliverable; omitting unknown/untested operations from limitations.
manual_remainder: business impact, final report review and deciding what to hand to the client. The acceptance harness simulates those operator decisions on synthetic data; it does not automate professional sign-off.
